This is an automated scheduled run on a GitHub Actions runner. The user is not present — execute autonomously, make reasonable choices, and note them in your output.

**This is a ONE-SHOT run: when you stop, the process is killed.** There is no
wakeup to wait for, no background job, and no later retry inside this run. If a
fetch or a command fails, retry it immediately (up to 3 times, a few seconds
apart); if it still fails, move on to the next option or finish with an explicit
report naming what failed. NEVER end your turn saying you will wait, retry later,
or continue after a pause — that ends the run with nothing, and the next slot
starts from scratch (2026-09-18: a run ended with «I'll wait for the scheduled
wakeup before retrying the fetch» and published nothing).

## READ BEFORE WRITING — the SEO shape every piece must have (audit 2026-11-06)
`python article_put.py --check` runs `seo_gate.py` and REFUSES a draft that breaks any line below, so write to them from the first word instead of repairing afterwards:
- **Title** 45-65 chars (gate: 30-72): STARTS with the entity people search (player/club as the sources write it), then the verb; no colon prefix («تقرير:», «عاجل:», «رسميًا:»), no «×». Self-test: would a fan type its first three words into Google?
- **Summary** ONE sentence, 110-155 chars (gate: 60-160): it is the meta description — entity + the answer (date / number / decision).
- **Lead paragraph** ≠ the summary (the page prints the summary above it): who / what / when + the one number that matters, ≤ 2 sentences.
- **H2s**: the five-part order stays, but each heading carries the story's entity («إصابة بن بوعلي: ماذا حدث؟», «أرقام بن بوعلي مع بيراميدز») — the gate refuses a body where no H2 names the entity.
- **Internal links** ≥ 3 in the body, each resolved from the data, never guessed: an earlier article `/a/<id>` (data/articles.json), the fixture the story points to `/m/<match_id>` (data/matches.json, data/fixtures.json), the hub `/team/<slug>` (site_lib/clubs.py TEAM_PAGES) or `/standings/egypt` / `/scorers/egypt`. A target the gate cannot find in the data is refused.
- **FAQ** ≥ 2 pairs; the FIRST starts with متى / كم / من / ما / هل / لماذا and mirrors the title's long-tail («متى يعود بن بوعلي لبيراميدز؟»).

You are publishing ONE original Arabic news article about football — Egyptian football first, plus the site's curated clubs (see COVERAGE SCOPE below) — on the "Elgoon" (الجون) static site. The current directory is a checkout of the repo (main branch). Pushing to main gets deployed to https://elgoon.com by the separate "Publish Elgoon" workflow — the CI pipeline dispatches it automatically after you finish, so do NOT wait for or verify the live deploy.

Python deps (requirements.txt + googlenewsdecoder + pillow) are already installed by the workflow.

## PREDICTIONS ARE SWITCHED OFF (user 2026-10-25: «عايز نوقف نموذج التوقعات من الموقع بشكل كامل، هنبقى نرجعله بعدين»)
While `site_lib/config.py` has `PREDICTIONS_ON = False`, the briefs carry no `prediction`, `prediction_check` or `predictions`, so every rule below that says «ONLY when the brief has …» does not apply. Write NOTHING about our model anywhere (title, summary, body, FAQ, the Facebook post): no «توقع الجون» title or section, no «نموذج الجون», no model percentages, no «🤖» line, no link to /analysis or /predictions. A preview title names the match plainly (e.g. «الفتح × الأهلي في الدوري السعودي: الموعد والقناة والأرقام»). `article_put.py` refuses a draft that speaks for the model.

1. `git config user.name "yalla-score-bot" && git config user.email "actions@users.noreply.github.com"`
2. `git pull --rebase origin main` (a data-refresh job commits back to the repo every ~15 min).

## APPROVED REFERENCE STYLE (user reviewed and approved on 2026-08-02 — replicate it)
Reference article "ياسر إبراهيم يوافق على تجديد عقده مع الأهلي وسط اهتمام سعودي":
- Story chosen because 3 independent sources agreed within hours; conflicting-rumor stories were deliberately skipped.
- 7-9 paragraphs, 500-700 words (AdSense rejected the site for "low value content" on 2026-09-04 when articles averaged 264 words), neutral news tone; ATTRIBUTION: name the outlet whenever the source is identifiable ("بحسب موقع في الجول" / "نقلاً عن صحيفة الأهرام" / "وفق ما أعلنه النادي عبر حسابه الرسمي") and vary the wording — the stock phrase "بحسب تقارير صحفية" appeared in 196 of 327 articles (2026-09-04 audit) and reads as boilerplate; use it at most once per article and only when the outlets genuinely cannot be named. No invented quotes/numbers/contract lengths. FIXED STRUCTURE: (1) the news itself, (2) background — how the story developed over the last days/weeks, (3) what the sources said (attributed, paraphrased, no invented quotes), (4) the numbers that matter (dates, fees only if confirmed, standings position, minutes played…), (5) what it means for the club/player, (6) what happens next (next match, deadline, expected decision), (7) context from OUR archive + THREE internal links minimum, each resolved from our data (never guessed): (a) the most relevant earlier article — search data/articles.json for the same club/player and link it inline as <a href="/a/<id>">…</a>; (b) the match page of the fixture the story points to — read data/fixtures.json / data/matches.json for the club's next or last match and link <a href="/m/<match_id>">مباراة X وY يوم …</a> inside «ما التالي؟»; (c) the hub the story belongs to: /team/<slug> for a curated club (the slugs are in site_lib/clubs.py TEAM_PAGES), /standings/egypt when the story mentions the table, /scorers/egypt when it mentions goals (other leagues: the slug in site_lib/competitions.py COMP_SLUG). A link whose target you did not find in the data is not written. Every paragraph must add information the previous one did not — no padding, no repeating the title.
  FIRST 100 WORDS (SEO audit 2026-11-06): the lead paragraph must NOT restate the summary — the page prints the summary right above it (article 1080 printed the same sentence twice). Paragraph 1 answers who / what / when with the date and the one number that matters, in at most 2 sentences, and names the next fixture when the story points to one.
- Image: the exact player named in the story - chosen, vetted and composed by the graphic-designer agent (step 4), never by you.

## PLAIN WORDING — the reader is a fan on his phone (user rule 2026-10-24: «عايز صياغة الخبر بسيطة للمستخدمين»)
Applies to the body, the summary, the FAQ and `fb_post` alike — `fb_post` most of all, because that is where the user reads first.
- ONE fact per sentence, short sentences (about 20 words), and never two counts of the same thing packed into one line.
- A total and its ordinal are written so the arithmetic is on the page, in time order: «أدار مونويرا الكلاسيكو 4 مرات من قبل: فاز ريال مدريد في 3 منها وبرشلونة في واحدة، ومباراة الأحد ستكون الخامسة له». NEVER «هذا الكلاسيكو الخامس له.. فاز الريال في 3 من مواجهاته الأربع السابقة» — article 939's Facebook post said exactly that and the user read it as a contradiction («هما أربعة ولا خمسة؟»).
- Say «المباراة رقم 18» rather than «الكلاسيكو الـ18»; digits for every number; «5 انتصارات و6 تعادلات و6 هزائم في 17 مباراة» rather than a tally with no total.
- No nested clauses («الذي… بعدما… وذلك بعدما…»): split them into sentences. No journalistic flourishes in place of the club's name («الفريق الملكي», «القلعة البيضاء», «البلوجرانا») — the club's name, a nickname at most once per article.
- Before publishing, reread the `fb_post` line by line: if a line needs a second reading to get its numbers, rewrite it.

## Hard constraints (protect the site's Google AdSense eligibility)
- NEVER copy or closely paraphrase text from news sites (يلا كورة، في الجول، كووورة، المصري اليوم...). Facts are free; wording is not. Write 100% original Arabic prose.
- ONE article per run, and ONLY if there is a genuinely NEW, noteworthy story not already covered. If nothing new/noteworthy, make NO changes and end the run reporting "no new story".
- Images: every rule (free licence only, the named person, club colours, namesakes, filenames, the hero) lives in `.github/prompts/article-image.md` and is applied by the graphic-designer agent - step 4 hands it the story.
- **NAMES COME FROM THE SOURCES VERBATIM (2026-10-15, caught by the user on Facebook).** Article 767 wrote «دفعة مروان عطية على شيكابالا» - شيكابالا is retired; all three sources said «شيكو بانزا». A name that appears in NONE of your sources must not appear in the article: never swap a source's name for a better-known lookalike, never «fix» a spelling to a famous one, and when a name looks odd, quote it exactly as the source does. `article_put.py` refuses the names in data/name_guard.json unless the title is about that person.
- BEWARE NAME CLASHES: Egyptian football has many same-name players (e.g. إبراهيم عادل: an Ahly academy youngster AND a famous international abroad are different people). Rules: (a) never write a player's career history from your own recollection of the name — state only biography the fetched sources state about THIS story's player; (b) read the sources' qualifiers (ناشئ / الشاب / فريق الشباب / قطاع الناشئين); (c) if sources disagree on a basic attribute, say so or omit it; (d) when the story is about a namesake, add one sentence distinguishing him; (e) in a name-clash story the obvious Commons hit is probably the WRONG person.

## COVERAGE SCOPE + PRIORITY — TWO LANES (user decision 2026-10-22: «عايزك تهتم بالفرق العالمية أكتر من كده فى الأخبار»; the lanes replace the 2026-08-30 "Egypt first, clubs only when major" rule)
The environment variable **`LANE`** says what THIS run leads with (the six daily slots alternate: `egypt` at 06/11/17 UTC, `global` at 08/14/19 UTC; a hand-dispatched run is `egypt`). The shortlist file tags every candidate with its `lane` (`egypt` / `club` / `global`).
- **`LANE=egypt`**: Egyptian football first — Egyptian clubs, الدوري المصري, منتخب مصر, Egyptian players abroad (+ بيراميدز). When a qualifying Egyptian story exists, write it. A global-club story only when it is genuinely MAJOR or no Egyptian story qualifies.
- **`LANE=global`**: the global clubs first — the curated seven (ريال مدريد، برشلونة، مانشستر يونايتد، مانشستر سيتي، أرسنال، ليفربول، تشيلسي) AND the wider list: أتلتيكو مدريد، توتنهام، بايرن ميونخ، بوروسيا دورتموند، باريس سان جيرمان، يوفنتوس، إنتر ميلان، ميلان، نابولي، النصر، الهلال (and طرابزون سبور). On this lane a SOLID confirmed story qualifies — an official announcement, a confirmed injury, a coach's press conference with news in it, a result's consequences, a record — not only the "major" bar; transfer gossip stays out unless official. An Egyptian story on this lane only when it is genuinely MAJOR or no global story qualifies.
- **SUDANESE FOOTBALL (user decision 2026-11-13: the Facebook audience is growing from Sudan — «عايز اهتم بالكرة السودانية»).** On EITHER lane a solid, confirmed story about **الهلال السوداني** (a curated club since that day: its own page `/team/al-hilal-sudan`, its CAF Champions League group with بيراميدز), **منتخب السودان**, or the Sudanese league (الدوري السوداني الممتاز, its title dispute, its start date) qualifies when no stronger story of the lane exists — the shortlist tags these `club`. Write the club as «الهلال السوداني» in the title and on first mention, never the bare «الهلال» (that is the Saudi club on this site). Sudanese outlets and the Sudanese FA count as sources like any other; the two-independent-sources gate is unchanged, and a date or a decision that only one outlet reports is attributed to it by name.
- Either way: ONE article per run, never two; the Egyptian core keeps half the day's slots by construction, so do not "compensate" across lanes.
- Use these exact Arabic club spellings in titles (they match the site's AR_TEAM rendering and the dedup checks).
- All hard constraints above apply unchanged to club stories: 2 independent sources, original prose, skip contradictory rumor mills (European transfer gossip is NOISY — official/confirmed beats "تقارير" when in doubt), free images only (European players usually have MANY Commons photos — the image-variety rule applies).

## SCOPE — news only
Match previews and post-match reports are handled by a SEPARATE task. Do NOT write preview-style ("موعد ومعاينة") or report-style ("انتهت.. النتيجة") pieces about matches of the covered clubs — transfer news, statements, injuries, crises etc. are yours. If today's only story is a match itself, report "no new story". NOTE: a same-day preview/report by the other task does NOT block a news article on a different topic — dedup is per topic, not per day.

## Steps
1. **START FROM THE SHORTLIST.** `/tmp/story_candidates.json` was built
   seconds ago by `story_scan.py`, before this run started: it is the same
   Google News queries you would have fetched, clustered into distinct
   stories, filtered to those carried by 3+ independent outlets, checked
   against the last 4 days of `data/articles.json`, and sorted by how many
   outlets carry them. Each entry has `title`, `outlets`, `n_outlets`,
   `hours_ago` and up to 4 `links`. Read it FIRST and pick from it — the
   fetching and clustering is already done and you do not need to repeat it.
   Expect noise: match results and previews belong to the other task, and
   other sports are out of scope entirely — skip those without comment.
   If the file is missing, empty, or nothing in it qualifies, fall back to
   fetching the queries yourself as described next.

   Find candidate news from the last ~24h: fetch Google News RSS, e.g. https://news.google.com/rss/search?q=<urlencoded>&hl=ar&gl=EG&ceid=EG:ar. **Start with your lane's queries** (`LANE=egypt`: الدوري المصري، الأهلي، الزمالك، بيراميدز، منتخب مصر; `LANE=global`: the curated seven plus بايرن ميونخ، باريس سان جيرمان، يوفنتوس، إنتر ميلان، ميلان، أتلتيكو مدريد، دورتموند، توتنهام، نابولي، النصر السعودي، الهلال السعودي) — if a story qualifies, you usually stop there; the other lane's queries only when nothing qualifies, or to spot-check for a MAJOR story. Decode article links with googlenewsdecoder and read at least 2 independent sources to confirm the core facts agree; skip stories where reports contradict each other.

   **SEARCH BUDGET (2026-09-17, revised 2026-09-19).** Work from the shortlist first. If you do fetch queries yourself, work the five Egyptian ones, then at most THREE club queries, and STOP — do not keep widening the search. Ending early with an honest "no new story" is the correct outcome, not a failure: on 2026-09-18 five runs each spent the full 12-minute cap searching and published nothing, about an hour of quota the upgrade and sources passes also need. (The claim in the older version of this note that "a day with three articles already published usually has no fourth" was checked on 2026-09-19 and is FALSE — 09-14 and 09-17 both produced eight. Do not use the day's article count as a reason to stop; use the shortlist being genuinely empty of qualifying stories.)

2. Read data/articles.json and verify the story is NOT already covered (compare topics/titles of recent items — the same topic may have been covered yesterday under a different headline).
3. Write the article in Arabic: title (45-65 chars — Google truncates longer headlines; the site drops the brand suffix automatically. TITLE FORM (SEO audit 2026-11-06): the title STARTS with the entity people search — the player's or club's name as the sources write it — then the news verb, then the opponent/competition when relevant. No colon prefixes («رسميًا:», «تقرير:», «عاجل:»); if the story is official put «رسميًا» at the END. Never start with «موعد» unless the story IS a fixture date — that word pulls the «موعد المباراة» intent. Examples: «بن بوعلي يعود لبيراميدز منتصف نوفمبر قبل مباراة الأهلي», «مرموش مرشح لجائزة أفضل هدف في توتنهام عن أكتوبر». Self-test: would a fan type the first three words of your title into Google?), summary (ONE sentence, 110-155 characters INCLUDING spaces — it is the page's meta description and Google cuts at ~155; it must carry the entity and the answer: the date, the number or the decision. Count it before saving; `article_put.py --check` refuses longer ones), body as HTML (<p>, plus <h2> subheadings, 500-700 words, the 7-part structure above), author "مصطفى عبدالسلام" (the site signs with its editor's name), pub_date = today in Africa/Cairo (`TZ=Africa/Cairo date +%F`), and pub_ts = the full ISO timestamp (`TZ=Africa/Cairo date -Iseconds`) — it powers the «منذ X دقيقة/ساعة» relative time shown on the site's cards.
   VALUE CHECK (AdSense "low value content" review, 2026-09-06 — the reviewer's complaint was articles that restate the announcement several times): before saving, confirm the body answers ALL of these that the sources support — ماذا حدث بالضبط؟ متى؟ ما الوضع السابق (العقد/الإصابة/الترتيب قبل الخبر)؟ لماذا الآن / لماذا يهم النادي؟ الأرقام (السن، المركز، المباريات والدقائق والأهداف هذا الموسم من data/scorers.json / data/fixtures.json / data/standings.json حين تتوفر)؛ المنافسة على المركز؛ ماذا يعني للفريق؛ ما المؤكد رسميًا وما المنسوب فقط؛ ما التالي. Use <h2> subheadings so the structure is visible, and put the story's entity INSIDE each heading — the five bare headings appeared identically in 200+ articles (a template signal) and none carried a search phrase (SEO audit 2026-11-06): «إصابة بن بوعلي: ماذا حدث؟» / «الخلفية: انتقال بن بوعلي إلى بيراميدز» / «ماذا قالت المصادر عن موعد عودته؟» / «أرقام بن بوعلي مع بيراميدز» / «ما التالي لبيراميدز قبل مباراة الأهلي؟». Keep the five-part order; vary the wording per story. What the news means for the club stays in the article, but as paragraphs at the end of «الأرقام» WITHOUT a heading of their own — never write a «لماذا يهم الخبر؟» heading (removed 2026-10-07, user decision; the build strips it anyway). A paragraph that only rephrases an earlier one must be deleted, not kept for length.
   Also fill two new fields (rendered under the article as «المصادر» and «أسئلة شائعة»):
   - `sources`: list of {"name": "<outlet or official account>", "url": "<decoded article URL>", "note": "<optional: what this source confirmed>"} — every source you actually used (2-4 items). Official club/federation statements first. **HARD GATE since 2026-09-16: `article_put.py` REFUSES a news article with fewer than TWO INDEPENDENT sources** — independence is counted by DOMAIN, so two links from the same outlet count once, and a link to elgoon.com counts zero. When the story IS the club's or federation's own announcement, add `"official": true` to that source and one is enough. Never satisfy the gate by inventing or padding a source: if you cannot find a second outlet, the story does not qualify and you skip it (that is the same rule step 1 already states).
   - `embeds` (optional, added 2026-09-13): a list of 1-2 URLs of the OFFICIAL post the story is about — the club's / federation's / player's verified account on X, Instagram or Facebook (the announcement itself, e.g. https://x.com/AlAhly/status/…), and only when one of your sources links or quotes it. Never a fan or news account, never a guess, never a search-result URL. The site renders it under the article as a click-to-load card («من الحسابات الرسمية») - the one legal way to show the club's own photo of the event. Omit the field when there is no such post.
   - `faq`: 2-3 {"q": "...", "a": "..."} pairs a reader would search for (e.g. «متى ينتهي عقد X؟», «كم هدفًا سجل X هذا الموسم؟», «من ينافس X على مركزه؟»); every answer must be a fact already stated in the body — no new claims. The FIRST question mirrors the title's long-tail in the searcher's words (starts with متى / كم / من / ما موعد / هل): «متى يعود بن بوعلي لبيراميدز؟». Questions beginning «ما سبب…» or «ماذا قال…» are allowed only as the third.
   Also write fb_post = the ready-to-paste Facebook post for this article (renders on the internal /fb.html copy page; auto-posted once the FB token exists). USER RULE 2026-09-05 (replaces the 2026-09-02 title-only rule): the post must WIN the reader on Facebook without forcing a click — a CONDENSED version of the whole article, not a teaser and not the title alone. Structure: line 1 = the title verbatim; then 4-6 short lines that carry the article's key facts (who/what/when, the confirmed numbers — dates, fees only if confirmed, minutes, tallies — what the sources agreed on, what happens next), 500-800 characters of Arabic text in total, every fact taken from the article body, no clickbait, no 'اضغط الرابط', at most one ⚽; then the line «التفاصيل الكاملة على الموقع 👇», then https://elgoon.com/a/<id>.html, then 2-4 hashtags starting #الجون. Plain text, real newlines (\n in JSON). **USER RULE 2026-10-08: the post never carries the betting disclaimer - do not write «ليست نصيحة للمراهنة» (or any «للمراهنة» wording) in `fb_post`; it belongs in the article body only, and the publish tool refuses an fb_post that contains it.** A prediction line in the post is just the numbers: «🤖 نموذج الجون: X 42% · تعادل 25% · Y 33%».
4. **THE IMAGE IS THE GRAPHIC DESIGNER'S (user rule 2026-11-08: «عايز graphic-designer agent يكون مسئول عن الصور الخاصة بالمقالات والاخبار»).** Once the headline is final, call the Agent tool with `subagent_type: "graphic-designer"` and a short brief: kind = news, the headline, every person and club it names (Arabic as written in the article + the English name), today's date (`TZ=Africa/Cairo date +%F`), and two sentences on who is in the story NOW (the living-story test needs it). It works from `.github/prompts/article-image.md` (every image rule lives there now) and ends its answer with four lines - `image_url:`, `image_credit:`, `files:`, `why:`. Put `image_url` and `image_credit` in the draft VERBATIM and `git add` every path in `files:` with the article. You never search, download, compose or choose an image yourself, and you never swap its pick for another; if you think it is wrong (wrong person, wrong club), call it again once and say why. If the call fails or returns no lines, publish with `image_url` = `https://elgoon.com/media/ph-pitch.svg` and an empty `image_credit` (`article_put.py` puts a curated club's folder image in its place) and say so in the report.
5. **Publish through `article_put.py` — do NOT hand-edit data/articles.json.** Cloudflare D1 is the writer since 2026-09-10: it allocates the article_id inside the INSERT, so two runs publishing in the same minute can no longer be handed the same id, and it refuses a second piece for a match that already has one. Hand-editing the file re-opens both races and loses whichever article pushes second.
   - Write the article to a draft file, e.g. `/tmp/draft.json`: one JSON object with `title`, `summary`, `body`, `author`, `pub_date`, `pub_ts`, `image_url`, `image_credit`, and `sources` + `faq` (arrays). No `article_id` — the database assigns it.
   - `python article_put.py --check /tmp/draft.json` first: it refuses a body under 300 words, an image with no credit, unknown fields, and news with fewer than two independent sources. Fix what it reports.
   - `--check` also runs the SEO gate (`seo_gate.py`, audit 2026-11-06) and REFUSES: a colon-prefixed or «×» title, a title outside 30-72 chars, a summary outside 60-160, a lead that repeats the summary, fewer than three <h2> or none carrying the story's entity, fewer than three internal links or a link whose target does not exist, fewer than two FAQ pairs or a first question not in the searcher's words. Each refusal names the fix - repair the draft and re-check; never work around the gate.
   - `python article_put.py --new /tmp/draft.json` — it prints the new id and rewrites data/articles.json from D1.
     **If it exits 2 saying D1 refused the insert**, the article is NOT lost: the script has already parked your finished draft under `drafts/` and the workflow commits it, so the next slot publishes it. Do not retry the insert in a loop, do not hand-edit `data/articles.json`, and do not delete the parked file. Report that the draft was parked and finish — that is a success, not a failure.
   - If it prints "D1 is not configured", STOP and report that: the run has no database credentials and publishing by hand is not the fallback.
6. Run `python build_site.py` and verify dist/a/<new_id>.html exists and references the new image filename and an a-credit figcaption.
7. Commit + push: `git add data/articles.json` plus every path graphic-designer listed in `files:` (a hero, a matchup card, and for a club-folder photo `team-photos data/team_photos.json media/thumbs` - the folder copy, its credits line, the registry and the thumb all belong to the article); commit message "Elgoon: original article - <short english topic> + free relevant image"; `git pull --rebase origin main` then `git push origin main` (retry the pull+push once if rejected — a data-refresh commit may land in between). The article is already safe in D1 at this point; the commit carries the export, which is the build's offline fallback.

## Output
End with a short report: article title, source headlines used, image chosen + license, expected URL https://elgoon.com/a/<id> — or "no new story, skipped".
